instructions: The marks are indicated in the right-hand margin.
There are NINE questions in this paper.
Assume any suitable data, if required.

sections.section_title: Q.1 Define the following in short, preferably one or two sentences each (any seven) :

questions.text: Fluid
Guide vanes
Draft tube
Turbo means
Hydraulic turbine
Stay ring
Mechanical efficiency
Specific speed
Centrifugal pump
Manometric head
Explain the classification of fluid machineries.
Briefly explain the different types of turbine and write the advantages of each.

A \( 40\text{ m/s} \) velocity jet of water strikes without shock a series of vanes moving at \( 10\text{ m/s} \). The jet is inclined at an angle of \( 20^\circ \) to the direction of motion of vanes. The relative velocity of jet at outlet is 0.9 times of the value at inlet and the absolute velocity of water at exit is to be normal to the motion of vanes. Determine (i) the vane angles at entrance and exit, (ii) the work done on vanes per second per N of water supplied by the jet and (iii) the hydraulic efficiency.
Show that the efficiency of a Pelton wheel will be maximum when the velocity of the wheel is half the velocity of the jet of water at inlet.

An inward flow reaction turbine having an overall efficiency of 80% is required to deliver \( 136\text{ kW} \). The head \( H \) is \( 16\text{ m} \) and the peripheral velocity is \( 3.3(H)^{0.5} \). The radial velocity of flow at inlet is \( 1.1(H)^{0.5} \). The runner rotates at \( 120\text{ r.p.m.} \) The hydraulic losses in the turbine are 15% of the available energy. Determine (i) the diameter of the runner, (ii) the guide vane angle, (iii) the runner blade angle at inlet and through the turbine. Assume the discharge from the runner is radial.
Explain the purpose of providing (i) scroll casing, (ii) stay vanes and (iii) guide vanes for a reaction turbine.

A Pelton wheel has to develop \( 13230\text{ kW} \) under a net head of \( 800\text{ m} \) while running at a speed of \( 600\text{ r.p.m.} \) If the coefficient of the jet \( C_v = 0.97 \), speed ratio \( \phi = 0.46 \) and the ratio of the jet diameter is \( \frac{1}{16} \) of the wheel diameter, calculate the number of jets required for the Pelton wheel. Also calculate (i) the diameter of jet, (ii) the diameter of pitch circle and (iii) the quantity of water supplied to the wheel.
Differentiate between centrifugal and reciprocating pump.

A centrifugal pump having an impeller \( 30\text{ cm} \) outside diameter rotates at \( 1050\text{ r.p.m.} \) The vanes are radial at exit and \( 7.5\text{ cm} \) wide. The velocity of radial flow through the impeller is \( 3\text{ m/s} \). The velocities in the suction and delivery pipes are \( 2.5\text{ m/s} \) and \( 1.5\text{ m/s} \) respectively. Neglecting frictional losses, determine the height through which the pump lifts, and the horsepower of the pump. Assume radial entry.
Explain the different efficiencies used in centrifugal pump.

A centrifugal pump lifts water against a static head of \( 40\text{ m} \) of which \( 4\text{ m} \) is suction. The suction and delivery pipes are both \( 15\text{ cm} \) in diameter. The head loss in the suction pipe is \( 2\text{ m} \) and in the delivery pipe \( 7.5\text{ m} \). The impeller is \( 40\text{ cm} \) in diameter, \( 2.5\text{ cm} \) wide and runs at \( 1250\text{ r.p.m.} \) The blade angle at exit is \( 30^\circ \). If the manometric efficiency is 80% and mechanical efficiency 70%, determine the power required to drive the pump and discharge.
